# BAD-046 — Split web/collabweb.js (1580 lines) into collabweb-<part>.js classic scripts

## Brief
Plan: [[docs/spikes/bad-036/web-collabweb|web-collabweb spike]] (Shepody, BADS-036).

Proposed: eight contiguous classic scripts at web/ top level, tagged between billing.js and start.js in line order: collabweb-model 259, host 235, seat 103, sync 221, modal 108, phases 267, tab 261, and collabweb.js kept as the last tag at 126. All 108 declarations are placed; the ?join= invite moves into collabweb.js so both writers of pendingInvite share a file. Three files over 250 are argued. Proven on a scratch copy: the concatenation matches fully and partly split, the check catches a rename and a missing use strict, and web-guest-mode.test.js passes 10 of 10 with the tag-derived file list (9 of 10 fail without it).

Cross-ticket: shares the tag-derived test helper and the duplicate-name sweep with the web/app.js and web/booth.js splits. Two stale comments inside the moved code (line 7, lines 81 to 82) are fixed in a separate commit after the move.

Verification: the concatenation check, npm test, npm run web:build, and a manual two-account npm run web:local pass, since hosting, joining and syncing have no automated coverage.

**Gate.** Queued until Eric approves the proposed file layout in the spike. Phase 2 does not start before that approval, and an approval that changes the layout is written into the spike's section 4 first.

**Rules for Phase 2, from BAD-036.** Split by responsibility; 250 lines is where a file gets a second look, not a cap, and every file left over 250 is argued in the spike's section 6. Every PR is a pure move: no statement is edited, a bug found on the way is its own ticket, and the spike's behaviour-preservation check (section 8) runs on every PR. The public surface in section 2 is the compatibility contract and does not change. Extraction order follows section 9: shared constants, types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components or handlers, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator. Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier for the files touched, quoted in each PR.

## Size, persona and model decision
Eric's call, 2026-09-15: the spike's layout is approved as proposed (section 4 unchanged: collabweb-model.js 259 keeping the 29-line header, -host 235, -seat 103, -sync 221, -modal 108, -phases 267, -tab 261, and collabweb.js kept as the last tag at 126 holding the ?join= invite and wireCollab; none of section 6's optional cuts, and not section 5's entry-first alternative), and Phase 2 lands as ONE pull request with one commit per section 9 step, each green on the section 8 concatenation check against the PR's base. One engineer on opus in a worktree on feat/bad-046-split-web-collabweb after bash scripts/worktree-init.sh, then a reviewer on opus (Fable's weekly limit is reached, Eric 2026-09-15) who reruns the concatenation check, the duplicate sweep and the load-order probes before it lands. No member, child or probe runs on fable. web/collabweb.js is byte-unchanged between the spike's revision 20d11e1 and origin/main 072153a, so the spike's line numbers hold; BAD-044 already added the group() helper to test/web-guest-mode.test.js, so step 1's harness edit is only pointing lines 237 and 454 at group('collabweb').
